title: Burst metering granularity and operator adjustment UI for misattributed surge charges
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Background:
Redwood Dedicated customers sometimes request manual invoice corrections after short-lived surge events. Current metering is aggregated to the hour for surge attribution which makes it hard to (a) identify short spikes that should be prorated, and (b) provide operators a safe way to correct misattributions without creating reconciliation drift.

Goal:
1) Increase burst/surge metering resolution to 1-minute granularity for the dedicated billing pipeline (configurable per-tenant).
2) Build an Operator Adjustment UI in Console that lets billing/ops team: view minute-level surge attribution, mark ranges for proration, apply manual crediting with audit trail, and queue reconciliations to regenerate invoices where needed.
3) Launch a server-side reconciler that can apply approved adjustments and produce an adjusted invoice delta with full auditability.

Non-goals:
- Change core pricing model (per-token) or automated customer-facing refund flows in this ticket.
- Replace existing automated surge smoothing heuristics (we will hook into them).

Approach and design notes:
- Metering changes:
  - Extend the metering ingest path to emit per-tenant per-fleet 1-minute rollups for: token_count, served_qps, surge_flag (boolean indicating request matched surge pool), and queue_time_ms.
  - Rollups to be stored in a new timeseries table (billing_minute_rollups) sharded by tenant_id and day. Retention default 90 days (configurable).
  - Backfill is NOT required for historical invoices. New resolution applies prospectively.

- Reconciler service:
  - New microservice billing-reconciler reads adjustment requests (approved by ops) and calculates prorated deltas. It will produce an adjustments artifact (CSV + JSON summary) and write to invoice-adjustments table.
  - Adjustments are idempotent and reference original invoice_id, meter_window_start, meter_window_end, operator_id, and reason_code.

- Operator UI (Console):
  - New page under Tenant > Billing > Surge adjustments. Primary view: time-series chart of minute-level surge attribution + table of candidate ranges flagged by heuristics (e.g., spike > 5x baseline within 10 minutes).
  - Actions: "Preview adjustment" (shows prorated credit), "Approve & schedule" (queues reconciler), "Apply now" (used for urgent corrections).
  - Every adjustment requires a free-text rationale and selection of an adjustment category (e.g., misattribution, billing-protection, negotiated-credit).
  - UI emits an audit event (immutable) and links to a generated adjustment artifact for finance.

- Heuristics and candidate generation:
  - A background job (surge-candidate-generator) scans minute rollups and emits candidate ranges where surge_fraction >= 0.6 and token_count > tenant_threshold over a sliding 15-minute window. Operators can edit ranges.

- API surface:
  - New endpoints: GET /v1/tenants/{id}/billing/minute-rollups?start=...&end=..., POST /v1/tenants/{id}/billing/adjustments (creates request), GET /v1/adjustments/{id}/preview, POST /v1/adjustments/{id}/approve. All endpoints require audit header and operator-id.

Acceptance criteria:
- Metering pipeline emits 1-minute rollups for a test tenant and data appears in billing_minute_rollups within 90s of event ingestion for 95% of samples.
- Console page renders minute series for selected tenant and shows candidate ranges from generator.
- Operator can create an adjustment, preview delta, and approve it. The reconciler consumes the approval and writes adjustment artifact.
- Audit trail stored; finance can download CSV for each adjustment.
- Unit/integration tests cover reconciliation math, idempotency, and permission checks.

Metrics to monitor:
- Ingestion latency (target 95th percentile < 120s for minute rollups).
- Number of adjustments created per week and average delta amount.
- Time between approval and reconciler completion (SLO: 10 minutes for small adjustments).

Risks and mitigations:
- Storage blowup: minute rollups increase billable storage. Mitigate by default 90-day retention and tenant-configurable resolution (tenants below threshold keep hourly).
- Reconciliation complexity: incorrect prorating could cause double credits. Use idempotency keys, immutable artifacts, and a two-phase apply (preview -> approve -> apply) to avoid mistakes.
- Abuse: operators must have RBAC + audit; require 'billing.adjust' permission.

Rollout plan:
1) Feature flag minute-rollups at tenant-level; enable for internal test tenants.
2) Deploy reconciler in canary mode (internal users) and run synthetic test adjustments against a sandbox tenant.
3) Release Operator UI behind admin-permission gate to a small pilot set.
4) Open to limited customer ops teams after 2 weeks of stable metrics.

Test plan:
- Integration: synthetic tenant emits spike events; verify rollups, candidate generator, UI preview, reconciler applies expected delta.
- E2E: simulate operator approving adjustment; verify invoice delta artifact and CSV format.
- Security: verify RBAC enforced and audit events immutable.

Open questions / decisions needed:
- Final default retention window for minute rollups for customers on Standard tier vs Enterprise (ops asked for 90/365). (Decide by 2026-03-10)
- Should reconciler auto-emit a customer-facing credit note or only internal artifacts? (Finance preference needed)

Documentation and artifacts:
- PRD: https://docs.redwood.ai/prd/dedicated/burst-metering-operator-ui (internal)
